93aab5ddf45a440cab5a5237402cc69e.title: Semi & Memory + AI — Q1 2026 directional thesis (12M)
93aab5ddf45a440cab5a5237402cc69e.body: Global semiconductor and memory sector long-thesis framework for Q1 2026 with 12-month horizon. Top-down structure: macro / cycle → sub-segment mechanics → equity name funnel. Framework is designed for a human researcher to determine cycle position, sub-segment ranking, geographic ranking, and candidate selection by walking the diagnostic question tree. The framework does NOT pre-decide any of these — the analyst's reading of the populated instruments determines the answer.
93aab5ddf45a440cab5a5237402cc69e.key_question: Given the framework's diagnostic outputs across cycle / sub-segment / geopol, what sub-segment(s) + name(s) deserve a long allocation and at what sizing within a 12% gross / 3% per-name risk budget?
93aab5ddf45a440cab5a5237402cc69e.inversion: If the framework's diagnostic chain returns no clear cycle-position signal AND no sub-segment with a defensible long-leg, then the right answer is no semi exposure — not a forced allocation.

a1f377ed6d9349e185f6e64271aa9553.title: What must be true for the long thesis to hold
a1f377ed6d9349e185f6e64271aa9553.body: Six structural drivers must hold for a long allocation to make sense. Each drives a sub-segment differently; the framework decomposes which drivers are most binding given current observable state.
a1f377ed6d9349e185f6e64271aa9553.key_question: Which of the 6 drivers are currently the binding constraint, and which are likely to remain so over the 12M horizon?
a1f377ed6d9349e185f6e64271aa9553.inversion: If 2 of 6 drivers turn against the thesis, the long case becomes untenable at the framework's risk budget (3% NAV per name).

dd8d7f0abef54f71909bf7822d814178.title: What would kill the long thesis
dd8d7f0abef54f71909bf7822d814178.body: Cycle-turn, geopol, supply-overbuild, and demand-air-pocket scenarios. Each scenario is stress-tested with explicit triggers, mechanisms, impacts, and observable signals. The framework holds the analyst responsible for re-running each scenario quarterly against fresh data.
dd8d7f0abef54f71909bf7822d814178.key_question: Which kill-chain triggers are most likely to fire within 12M, and what's the analyst's pre-committed action at each?
dd8d7f0abef54f71909bf7822d814178.inversion: If no kill-chain scenarios have triggers reaching the warning threshold over the analyst's monitoring window, conviction can rise from MEDIUM toward HIGH.

562802596943469c887ec4ba48a1e662.title: What's already priced in
562802596943469c887ec4ba48a1e662.body: Consensus, market-implied, gap-to-fundamentals, positioning, and narrative — each decomposed so the analyst can identify where the framework's diagnostic disagrees with consensus and where the asymmetry sits.
562802596943469c887ec4ba48a1e662.key_question: How many basis points of multiple expansion is consensus baking in for the AI-leveraged cohort vs. cycle-leveraged cohort, and how does that compare to the framework's read of cycle position?
562802596943469c887ec4ba48a1e662.inversion: If consensus already prices in the framework's bull case and the framework still reads early-cycle, the asymmetry favors leaving the position on; if consensus prices in late-cycle and the framework reads early, that's the highest-conviction setup.

79f1605d34c942b4b07675f3380603bf.title: How do we monitor
79f1605d34c942b4b07675f3380603bf.body: The lead / coincident / lag / scheduled / unscheduled / tripwire / cross-asset monitoring spine. Every must_be_true driver, every kill-chain scenario, and every priced-in consensus has at least one instrument under this pillar that resolves it on a defined cadence.
79f1605d34c942b4b07675f3380603bf.key_question: Are the lead/coincident/tripwire signals currently aligned with the must-be-true side, or showing divergence?
79f1605d34c942b4b07675f3380603bf.inversion: If this pillar's content is inconsistent or stale, the framework's kill-chains have no enforcement and the analyst is flying blind.

d44c7c7a4a274a359e54ea03eb812711.title: Macro: industry cycle + AI demand + geopol baseline
d44c7c7a4a274a359e54ea03eb812711.body: Six top-down drivers that must hold for a 12M long thesis on the semi & memory sector. Each driver has lead/coincident/tripwire metrics; the analyst walks the chain to determine which is binding now and which is likely to flip first.

ee1f582494574108941d05668bbe5eb6.title: Driver M1: AI accelerator unit demand sustains >25% YoY through 2026
ee1f582494574108941d05668bbe5eb6.body: AI accelerator unit demand is the load-bearing driver for the whole long thesis: every other observable — HBM tightness, CoWoS bottleneck, TSMC HPC mix, NVDA DC GM — is downstream of whether hyperscaler-5 (MSFT, GOOG, META, AMZN, ORCL) FY26 capex of ~$420bn aggregate converts into real GPU + custom-ASIC ship volumes growing 35-45% YoY by unit (per consensus Bloomberg/FactSet supply-side build). The framework must disaggregate genuine end-deployment from (a) hyperscaler capacity hoarding, (b) sovereign AI speculative procurement (UAE G42, Saudi PIF, India, EU AI Factories), and (c) order-book stuffing inflated by allocation behaviour. Sell-side cross-checks: NVDA DC QoQ revenue trajectory, NVDA purchase-commitment / fwd-revenue ratio, H100/H200 secondary-market pricing (rumour ~$20-25k H100 PCIe in 2026 vs $30k+ a year ago), and the ratio of custom-ASIC (TPU, Trainium, MAIA, MTIA) to merchant-GPU deployments. If accelerator units sustain >25% YoY and hyperscaler AI-infra share of capex stays above 55%, NVDA/AMD/AVGO are still on the up-leg of an earnings cycle; if either breaks, the multiple-led tape de-rates fast.

ae1f5a6177f449e3a02112c0044ff4c2.title: Driver M2: HBM allocation phase persists; HBM4 transition on-schedule
ae1f5a6177f449e3a02112c0044ff4c2.body: HBM is the single most pricing-elastic memory segment and the cleanest read-through on AI demand. Bit-supply growth from Hynix + Samsung + Micron — guided ~35-40% YoY based on stated capex + announced TSV/wafer capacity adds — vs bit-demand growth of >50% (per TrendForce and stated NVDA/AMD GPU + ASIC volumes) determines whether DRAM blended ASP holds. HBM3E shipped in volume through 2025 with Hynix at ~50%+ NVDA share and Samsung still chasing qualification in scale; HBM4 transition (3nm-class base die, 16-Hi stacks) ramps in 2H26 — Park's domain to verify yield curve. The 3:1 bit-output dilution from converting commodity DRAM wafers to HBM (per Hynix disclosure) means every HBM expansion tightens commodity DRAM. Framework holds if HBM ASP premium vs DDR5 sustains >5x (TrendForce quarterly) and HBM revenue at Hynix stays >50% of total DRAM; framework fails if Samsung achieves NVDA HBM3E qualification in scale (>20% share) before HBM4 absorbs the slack.

2feadb8e57a8420b808d18b50093615a.title: Driver M3: Commodity DRAM + NAND recovery slope holds 10-15%+
2feadb8e57a8420b808d18b50093615a.body: Commodity DRAM (DDR5/DDR4/LPDDR) and NAND form the lag-cycle leg of the memory complex. Non-HBM DRAM ASP inflected positive in Q3 2025 per TrendForce contract reads; the question for the next 12M is whether bit-demand from server (non-AI), mobile, and PC recovers to historical 15-20% YoY or stays at recession-grade 8-10%. The framework holds if (a) DRAM spot DDR5 16Gb prints >0% MoM sustained, (b) NAND TLC 512Gb wafer prices firm 1H26 (NAND lags DRAM ~1 quarter), and (c) the HBM-conversion dilution from Driver M2 keeps commodity bit supply growth subdued (sub-12% vs demand 10-15%). Sell-side risk is Samsung accelerating commodity DRAM capacity in 2H26 if their HBM3E qualification path slips. Macro layer: Compustat/FactSet top-50 semi WoI <14 weeks aggregate is the cleanest single read on the commodity-cycle exit; Tier-2 names (Samsung Memory standalone, Kioxia, SanDisk, WDC, Nanya, Winbond) are pure-play levered to this leg.

4e02c211261d4dd2b7028be3c7d8d8b8.title: Driver M4: Leading-edge fab utilization stays bifurcated (>90% N3/N2, 75-85% mature)
4e02c211261d4dd2b7028be3c7d8d8b8.body:
Bifurcation is the central structural feature of 2026 logic capacity: TSMC N3/N5 utilization is qualitatively 'tight' / 'fully utilized' per Q4 2025 call language, with HPC mix at ~52% of revenue and rising — that's the AI-leveraged leading-edge story. Mature node (N7-N16) utilization is in a 75-85% trough — that's the analog/MCU/auto-discrete story Priya covers from the demand side. The framework must quantify revenue mix at each foundry (TSMC, Samsung Foundry within 005930, Intel Foundry, SMIC, UMC, GlobalFoundries, Hua Hong, Vanguard, PSMC) and the dollar-content uplift from N2 ramp. Sell-side base case: TSMC monthly revenue YoY stays >15% through 2026, sequential growth holds above -5% in non-seasonal months, and HPC % of revenue does not roll over QoQ. Risks: (a) Samsung Foundry yield recovery to credible dual-source enables Apple A20-class moves, compressing TSMC N2 ASP; (b) Intel 18A credibility for AI customers (key Park / Mark cross-check).

Phase-5 reconciliation (David M4 vs Mark I6 - critic flagged): the original M4 framing of 'TSMC N3/N5 fully utilized' over-states the wafer-side constraint. Mark's I6 shows TSMC has some N3/N5 wafer slack in 2026; the binding 2026 AI constraint is CoWoS-L packaging (60-72k WEM canonical, see I6). Operative form of M4: leading-edge REVENUE stays tight at >90% N3/N2 utilization via the packaging-deliverability gate (CoWoS-L bounded above by I6), NOT via raw wafer capacity binding. Tripwire reading shifts: TSMC monthly YoY <15% should be interpreted as packaging-gated revenue softness, not wafer-demand softness. Wafer-side utilization is bounded above by packaging capacity.

da1b9db69bc647e0a3f704d57b31196b.title: Driver M5: CoWoS-L capacity expansion outpaces accelerator unit growth
da1b9db69bc647e0a3f704d57b31196b.body:
CoWoS-L (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate, TSMC) is the single binding bottleneck on AI accelerator unit deliverability through at least 1H26 per channel reads and DigiTimes. TSMC's stated capacity build path targets >50k wafer-equivalents/month by mid-2026 vs 2025 baseline of ~32-35k (rough channel synthesis — Mark will pin precise numbers). Macro framing: if CoWoS expands faster than accelerator unit demand growth, NVDA + AMD + AVGO custom-ASIC + Marvell ship volumes can fully convert order book to revenue and the M1 AI demand driver translates into earnings cleanly; if CoWoS lags, M1 demand shows up as guide-but-not-ship and the cycle inverts. The framework also tracks second-tier OSAT spill — ASE / Amkor advanced packaging revenue growth — as the diagnostic on whether TSMC is sole bottleneck or supply unlocking. Mark's domain owns the photolithography vs organic substrate vs RDL bottleneck decomposition; this driver node sits at macro-context tier.

Phase-5 direction correction (Priya Phase-4 critic): the original M5 KILL chain implied 'CoWoS slip -> rotate INTO memory' (treats memory as beneficiary of accelerator constraint). This is direction-inverted. Mechanism: HBM is bottle-fed into completed CoWoS assemblies, not into wafers. If CoWoS slips, HBM stacks at Hynix/Samsung/MU sit UNSOLD (no accelerator pull-through), ASP discipline cracks via stranded-stack destock, and Hynix bit-output is HURT, not helped. The KILL chain's then_breaks now correctly includes I1, Hynix, and MU alongside NVDA/AVGO. Mark's I6 fill has this directioning correct; M5 (this node) was misaligned pre-Phase-5.

37c4f86568654ecaa95c1b151523b691.title: Industry: sub-segment mechanics (memory / logic / equipment / packaging)
37c4f86568654ecaa95c1b151523b691.body: Sub-segment decomposition. Seven mechanics: HBM, commodity DRAM, NAND, leading-edge logic foundry, wafer-fab-equipment, advanced packaging (CoWoS / hybrid bonding), fabless AI accelerator. Each mechanic has its own cycle dynamics; aggregating them into 'memory' or 'logic' is the cardinal analytical error the framework prevents.

9ec54758e753489594912b5ee6cc4e92.title: Mechanic I1: HBM (HBM3e / HBM4) — allocation-driven, decoupled from commodity DRAM
9ec54758e753489594912b5ee6cc4e92.body: HBM is no longer part of the memory cycle - it is a separate market with its own supply curve (~3 qualified suppliers vs 5-6 in NAND), its own demand curve (4 accelerator buyers: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom-via-ASIC, Google/AWS via ASIC), and its own ASP discipline set by negotiation not spot. HBM3e 2025 baseline share: SK Hynix ~50-55%, Samsung ~25-30%, Micron ~15-20%; HBM ASP runs $15-25/Gb vs commodity DDR5 contract $3-4/Gb, a 4-6x premium that is the gross-margin engine for the entire memory complex. The 2-3x capex-per-bit cost of HBM (TSV etch + plating, micro-bump or hybrid bonding, KGSD test, base-die logic at TSMC N4/N3 for HBM4) means every Gb of HBM displaces ~2-3 Gb of conventional DRAM bit-output from the same wafer-start budget - HBM is structurally cannibalizing commodity DRAM supply, which is the most underappreciated reason commodity DRAM stayed disciplined post-2023. HBM4 base-die moves to TSMC foundry (N4/N3) introducing a foundry dependency on top of TSV+stacking yields, and KGSD (Known-Good-Stacked-Die) test capacity is a more binding bottleneck than wafer capacity. Cycle position now: still allocation-driven for HBM3e 12-Hi; HBM4 qualification window over the next 6-12 months determines 2027 share. The single swing variable is Samsung HBM3e 12-Hi qualification at Nvidia - if Samsung scales there, 3-supplier real competition emerges for the first time and HBM ASP discipline cracks.

9b1f4e026d6e49c1bdc9c8e148d8f04f.title: Mechanic I2: Commodity DRAM (DDR5 / DDR4 / LPDDR5X)
9b1f4e026d6e49c1bdc9c8e148d8f04f.body: Commodity DRAM is the cyclical leg of the memory complex - spot + contract pricing, inventory-driven, 30-50% peak-to-trough ASP swings. 2025-2026 starting state: recovering from 2022-2023 trough but NOT in shortage. Bit-demand growth ~10-15% YoY is the framework's base case, decomposed as server DDR5 RDIMM ~40-45% of bits (highest ASP, growing share, AI-server bonus 4-8x DRAM per box), mobile LPDDR5X ~35-40% (stable bit share, declining revenue share), PC ~10-15% (cyclical), graphics GDDR6X/GDDR7 ~5%. Bit-supply growth YoY ~10-12% is held down by the 3:1 wafer cannibalization to HBM (covered in I1) and post-2023 capex discipline at SKH+Samsung+Micron. Net cycle balance: capacity-to-demand ratio ~1.00-1.05, balanced trending toward tightening if HBM keeps absorbing wafer-starts. The wild card is CXMT (Changxin Memory): estimated 200-300k wpm in 2025 targeting 300-400k wpm by 2027, mostly DDR4 19nm/17nm-class - NOT competitive at DDR5 leading node yet, but the framework needs a tripwire on CXMT DDR5 sampling status. Contract ASP DDR5 16Gb at $3-4/Gb with spot lower in oversupply, spot leading contract by 4-8 weeks. Inventory weeks at SKH+Samsung: rule of thumb is <8 weeks undersupply, 8-12 balanced, 12-16 building, >16 oversupply - mid-2026 reads 8-10 weeks (balanced, tightening trajectory).

03032a27b041423e99c317461f7b5fbe.title: Mechanic I3: NAND (TLC / QLC, eSSD / cSSD)
03032a27b041423e99c317461f7b5fbe.body: NAND is the structurally-worst-disciplined of the three memory cycles - 5-6 suppliers vs 3 in DRAM (Samsung, SK Hynix+Solidigm, Micron, Kioxia, SanDisk, YMTC), lower switching costs, fast capex re-entry. The cycle character: layer-count race (232L baseline 2024-2025, 286L/300L+ ramping 2025-2026, 400L+ roadmap 2027-2028) compresses $/Gb ~15-20% per year and forces string-stack architectures (2-stack/3-stack); supply growth has decelerated from the 30-40%-per-year layer-add era but capex elasticity remains worst-in-class. Demand decomposition: AI eSSD (32TB/64TB/128TB QLC drives for training datasets and inference vector stores) is the bullish new vector (Solidigm 122TB and Samsung 128TB QLC already shipping); smartphone NAND content (stable bit, declining revenue mix); PC SSD content (weakest, recession-sensitive); enterprise eSSD pull from hyperscalers is real. The key swing variable is eSSD-to-cSSD ASP premium - healthy state is 50-100% per Gb premium (eSSD over cSSD wafer); compressed state is <30% premium, at which point the AI-NAND thesis is broken. QLC adoption is the second variable: AI eSSD's read-heavy workloads are perfect QLC fits, and the bit-density advantage (~33% over TLC) gives QLC-heavy suppliers (Solidigm by design, Micron mid, Samsung less) the AI-cost-leadership. Structural overhang: Kioxia post-2024 IPO capex behavior is a 2026-2027 watch-item; SanDisk post-WD-spin runs independently or merges (the Kioxia-SanDisk merger is the single biggest possible NAND-cycle event - would compress 5-6 suppliers to 4-5 and materially improve discipline). YMTC capacity-constrained by export controls at ~150-200k wpm, Chinese domestic only - NOT a leading-edge global threat. NAND ASPs improving 2025-2026 but lag DRAM ~1 quarter and stay weakest of the 3 cycles.

c763007fd35a48a7be6d48a9ec0c4edf.title: Mechanic I4: Leading-edge logic foundry (TSMC N3/N2/A16, Samsung 2nm, Intel 18A)
c763007fd35a48a7be6d48a9ec0c4edf.body: Leading-edge logic capacity is structurally TSMC-monopoly through 2026. TSMC N3 family (N3/N3E/N3P/N3X) is in mass production and fully utilized for Blackwell B100/B200/B300, Apple M-class, AMD MI350/MI355X; N2 (GAA nanosheet) is in risk production with HVM ramp guided 2H 2026; A16 (1.6nm with BSPD Super-Power-Rail) at pilot tools in F20 Hsinchu with HVM 2027. Samsung Foundry SF3 (3GAP) is shipping at materially impaired yield (reports of <50% on N+2-equivalent through Q4 2025); SF2 customer qualification at scale unconfirmed. 7620f5f64d45476d94f0738e5e8a3d45.title: Mechanic I6: Advanced packaging — CoWoS-L (TSMC), hybrid bonding (BESI), ABF substrate (Ibiden)
7620f5f64d45476d94f0738e5e8a3d45.body:
Advanced packaging - not leading-edge wafer capacity - is the binding constraint on AI accelerator deliverability in 2026 and the under-priced angle in Mark's contrarian framing. TSMC CoWoS wafer-equivalent monthly (WEM) capacity stepped 15k (YE 2023) -> 32k (YE 2024) -> ~60-65k actual vs ~70-75k guide (YE 2025) -> 110-130k guided (YE 2026). CoWoS-L (with LSI bridge in RDL substrate) is ~55% of 2026 capacity and the SPECIFIC bottleneck for Nvidia B100/B200/B300/GB200/Rubin; CoWoS-S (silicon interposer, ~30%) is for older H100/H200; CoWoS-R (RDL only, ~15%) for lower-perf AI / advanced HPC. Allocation politics renegotiated quarterly: Nvidia ~60-65% of CoWoS-L pool, AMD ~12-15% (MI300/325/350/355X), Broadcom (Google TPU + Meta MTIA + ByteDance ASIC) ~15-20%, with AWS Trainium 3 competing for the same pool from 2026. The hybrid bonding next-wave (Cu-Cu direct bonding, <1um pitch, no microbump) enables HBM4 base-die integration and chip-on-chip stacking - BESI is the dominant supplier (quasi-monopoly with AMAT as 2nd source), the cleanest mid-cap pure-play in the entire framework. The under-appreciated bottleneck on top of CoWoS WEM is ABF substrate: Ajinomoto sole-source for the build-up film; Ibiden (Japan), Unimicron (Taiwan), Nan Ya PCB, Shinko, AT&S do the lamination + drilling + build-up - capacity adds are slow because the lamination/drilling equipment is specialized and AI-grade substrates (large body, complex stackup) take ~3x longer to build than commodity. Rolling ABF shortages for AI accelerator packages were chronic 2024-2025; 2026 remains tight. The framework should treat I6 as a separate sub-segment from I5 (not 'equipment ex-litho'): the binding constraint is substrate + LSI bridge yield + KGSD test capacity, not lithography.

Phase-5 reconciliation (Mark canonical, applied tree-wide): the 2026 CoWoS-L corridor is 60-72k WEM, NOT 75k. 55% L-share x 110-130k total CoWoS = 60-72k CoWoS-L. Mid 66k. Priya's pre-fix 75k assumption shifted to 66k; NVDA bull PT math, AVGO custom-ASIC unit forecast, and Park HBM4 base-die scheduling priority all respect this corridor. Departures require explicit metadata.cowos_l_wem_assumption override.

b5a7c6dda17347b9b6096987353c2b2f.title: Mechanic I7: Fabless AI accelerator (NVDA / AMD / AVGO / MRVL / custom)
b5a7c6dda17347b9b6096987353c2b2f.body: Fabless AI accelerator is the demand-side capture layer that converts hyperscaler capex into merchant-silicon revenue. Three sub-tracks - each with different supply paths, different share trajectories, different margin profiles - which the framework MUST keep separate. Sub-track A: Nvidia merchant GPU. Hopper (H100/H200) tail ~1.0M units FY26; Blackwell (B100/B200/B300 + GB200/GB300 NVL72) ramp ~2.5-3.0M unit-equivalents FY26 base case; Rubin pre-orders FY26 H2 with HVM FY27. Nvidia datacenter revenue $130-160bn FY26 base, $115bn bear, $180bn bull. Datacenter GM 74-78% (the consensus is 76% midpoint; this is THE single most consequential GM line in the framework because every 100bps of compression = ~$2bn EBIT = ~3% of consensus EPS). Sub-track B: AMD merchant GPU. MI300X tail + MI325X + MI350 + MI400 (Helios) Late-FY26. Datacenter accelerator revenue $9-13bn FY26 (vs Lisa Su $14-18bn guide indication); the read on AMD is share-gain-vs-Nvidia not absolute number. Sub-track C: Custom ASIC partner-silicon (AVGO + MRVL + Alchip + GUC). AVGO Google TPU (v5/v6/v7) + Meta MTIA (v2/v3) + ByteDance ASIC + emerging Apple AI chip; MRVL AWS Trainium 2/3 + Inferentia. AVGO semi rev $60bn FY26 base ($20bn AI ASIC + networking; $40bn legacy semi including VMware-consolidated software which is treated as semi-pure-play here for IIM purposes). Custom-silicon $ share trajectory FY25 ~25-30% of US Big Five accelerator $ -> FY26 base 32-37% -> FY27 base 38-45% (drift of 4-6 points/year; bull-Nvidia case is share holds 70-75%, bear-Nvidia is 60-65%). The single most consequential question for the entire framework: where does the custom-silicon share trajectory land - and the framework instrumentation requires a 5-signal composite (AWS 'efficiency' language, GOOG tech-infra capex %, Anthropic/OpenAI training-run hardware disclosures, NVDA 10-K top-4 customer concentration, AMD share commentary tone shift).

70415378cfcb497a9a7b316780626544.title: Equity: screening funnel + candidate ranking
70415378cfcb497a9a7b316780626544.body: Top-down screening funnel: required attributes → operationalization → universe → ranking → entry design. The candidate pool spans memory (SK Hynix / Micron / Samsung), foundry (TSMC), equipment (ASML), fabless AI (NVDA / AMD / AVGO) — anchor names per sub-segment. Framework's screen produces the rank order; analyst makes the picks.

48bbf1d8488843dab513669039601497.title: Required attributes (cycle-leverage + AI-leverage + geopol-discount)
48bbf1d8488843dab513669039601497.body: Required attributes for the framework's cohort: each candidate is scored on three sub-segment-specific attributes - (1) cycle-leverage (mid- vs late-cycle exposure, operationalized via book-to-bill, capex/revenue, ASP momentum); (2) AI-leverage (AI revenue purity + AI vs non-AI GM delta + CoWoS/HBM allocation share); (3) geopol-discount (Taiwan-fab dependency, China end-use exposure, consensus pricing vs framework's stress/tail scenario impact). The composite score combines these with the framework's cycle / sub-segment / geopol reads to produce the candidate rank order. Each attribute is operationalized non-generically - the screen rejects abstract criteria like 'low P/E' or 'AI-related' and requires explicit, observable thresholds with cycle-history-anchored bands.
48bbf1d8488843dab513669039601497.key_question: What attributes must the winning names have given the cycle / sub-segment / geopol reads from the framework?
48bbf1d8488843dab513669039601497.inversion: If the screen's required-attribute list is generic ('low P/E') it won't differentiate; framework requires sub-segment-specific attribute formulation.

17f85eb7ced64c09b3bbaf5ad0c2ec5a.title: TSMC (TSM) — anchor candidate
17f85eb7ced64c09b3bbaf5ad0c2ec5a.body: TSMC is the framework's anchor leading-edge logic + advanced packaging name and the single asset that captures BOTH macro drivers M4 (bifurcated fab utilization) AND M5 (CoWoS-L expansion) AND mechanics I4 (leading-edge monopoly) AND I6 (advanced packaging bottleneck) in a single P&L. Q4 2025 base: HPC ~52% of revenue rising, smartphone ~30%, IoT ~6%, auto ~6%, DCE ~1%, other ~5%. N3+N5 utilization 'tight'/'fully utilized', mature node (N7-N16) 75-85% in the destock trough. Capex 2026 guided $42-44bn (95%+ on advanced nodes + AP), AP6 and AP7 fab construction in Chiayi tracking to ~110-130k CoWoS WEM by YE2026. Pricing: N3 wafer ASP ~$18-22k, N2 ASP base case $22k (Mark/David) vs Street consensus $25-28k - the binary risk Street under-prices is Apple/NVDA willingness to dual-source if Samsung SF2 yield closes or Intel 18A external delivers. Blended GM 53-55% with HPC pricing power carrying the mix; CoWoS-L is the highest-incremental-margin add. Risks specific to TSMC: (1) Apple dual-source binary; (2) Intel 18A external revenue >$1bn binary; (3) Taiwan geopolitical tail (M6) is a permanent overhang on multiple; (4) currency - TWD/USD - and non-cash inventory writedowns. The candidate scoring: TSMC clears top-3 ranking on AI-leverage + cycle + pricing-power + valuation; only memory complex (Hynix) competes on pure AI-leverage score, only ASML competes on pricing-power monopoly. The right framing is TSM-as-AI-utility with packaging optionality, not TSM-as-cyclical-foundry.

dbf21b2f7e7b46e6993663cd5adefb27.title: Synthesis: TSMC captures the chain
dbf21b2f7e7b46e6993663cd5adefb27.body: TSMC is the single asset that mechanically converts M4 (bifurcated fab utilization, leading-edge tight + mature in trough) + M5 (CoWoS-L expansion outpacing accelerator unit growth) into reported earnings via two parallel monopoly P&L lines: (1) leading-edge HPC wafers - N3 utilization 'tight', N2 ramp 2H 2026 at $22-25k base ASP / $25-28k bull, blended HPC GM 55%+ and rising as mix shifts; (2) advanced packaging - CoWoS-L wafer-equivalent monthly stepping 60-65k -> 110-130k YE2026, pricing power because TSMC has no real competitor in 2.5D AI-accelerator packaging at scale (Samsung I-Cube and Intel Foveros are captive-or-niche). The single-sentence chain: M1 AI accelerator demand >25% YoY * hyperscaler-5 capex $420bn -> TSMC HPC wafer pull at N3/N2 tight utilization -> TSMC HPC revenue +30-40% YoY at sustained ASP -> TSMC CoWoS-L revenue +40-60% YoY at firm incremental margin -> TSMC blended GM 53-55% with HPC mix carrying the bridge -> TSMC FY26 EPS ~+25% YoY -> P/E 28-32x defensible into cycle peak. The inversion chain (Apple dual-source on Samsung SF2 OR Intel 18A external >$2bn OR CoWoS WEM ramp slip) breaks both monopoly legs simultaneously and is why TSM is more binary than its 'utility AI infra' characterization suggests.

ca0aac9dbacb42a2b961cd3fbb753f1f.title: TSMC - Revenue drivers
ca0aac9dbacb42a2b961cd3fbb753f1f.body: TSMC FY26 revenue bridge: HPC (~52% of revenue, projected 55-58% by YE2026) grows ~35-45% YoY driven by N3/N3P/N3X wafer pull from Blackwell/Rubin/MI355X + ramp of N2 in 2H 2026 + Apple SoC mix to N2; smartphone (~30%) grows ~10-15% YoY on Apple A20 N2 ramp; CoWoS-L advanced packaging revenue (~5-7% of consolidated currently, accelerating to ~10-12% by YE2026) grows ~50-70% YoY on WEM step from 60-65k to 110-130k at $5-7k revenue/WEM blended. Mature node (N7-N16, ~12-15% of revenue) flat-to-slightly-up on auto/MCU destock-end. Consolidated FY26 revenue growth tracks ~25-30% YoY at base case. The single largest swing variable is N2 ASP - $22k Mark base implies $X consolidated FY26-27 revenue path; $25k+ bull (consensus) implies 200-300bps higher GM run-rate. Second-largest swing is CoWoS WEM achievement - 110k vs 130k vs 90k determines AP revenue contribution between $8bn and $12bn FY26. Risks: (1) Apple dual-source SF2 -> -5% revenue from smartphone shift; (2) CoWoS WEM slip -> -3-5% revenue from AP delay; (3) FX (TWD strength) -1% revenue impact per 1% TWD up. The 'TSM AI utility' framing requires HPC revenue +35%+ to sustain into FY27.

ed647db08dd14d4484e2ab74cb935650.title: TSMC - Margin drivers
ed647db08dd14d4484e2ab74cb935650.body: TSMC FY26 OpM bridge: blended GM 53-55% guided (vs 53.1% FY24 and 53.5% FY25e), with HPC GM 55%+ pulling above smartphone GM 50% and mature-node GM 35-40%. The single largest GM engine is HPC mix-shift from ~52% to 55-58% by YE2026 - each percentage point of HPC mix adds ~30-50bps to blended GM. CoWoS-L is the next highest-incremental-GM segment (estimated 65%+ GM on advanced packaging vs 53% blended) - WEM step adds ~50-100bps to blended GM FY26 vs FY25. Cost levers: (1) N3 yield maturity drives GM accretion 2-3pp through the node lifecycle; (2) N2 ramp drags GM 200-300bps in 1H of HVM but recovers by 2H; (3) depreciation step-up from Arizona Fab 21 + Kumamoto JV adds 100-150bps drag through FY26-27 as facilities ramp under-utilized in early years. FX: ~85% USD revenue, ~30% USD COGS - every 1% TWD weakness adds ~0.4% to GM. Risks specific: (1) Apple SF2 dual-source - -200bps GM if 50% of A21 volume shifts away; (2) CoWoS WEM slip - -50-100bps GM from AP mix dilution; (3) Intel 18A external $1bn+ - HPC ASP pressure -200bps GM. Base case FY26 blended GM 54-55%, OpM 44-46% (depreciation drag).

bbba74a3cccf416a9f735f8bb0bf223a.title: TSMC - Multiple / re-rating drivers
bbba74a3cccf416a9f735f8bb0bf223a.body: TSMC trades at ~22-26x fwd P/E vs 10Y mean ~17x and cycle-trough ~12x - implying the market is paying ~30-50% premium to mean for the HPC-leverage + CoWoS-L monopoly. The P/E-vs-cycle frame is appropriate for TSM (unlike memory) because TSM EPS cyclicality is much lower than memory (peak-to-trough ~2-3x vs memory 5-10x). Re-rating drivers: (1) HPC mix lifting above 55% structurally re-rates blended GM to 55%+ steady-state, justifying 25-28x fwd P/E as fair-value; (2) CoWoS-L monopoly extends 12-18 months further than consensus assumes given Samsung/Intel packaging gap; (3) Taiwan geopolitical risk premium compression as Arizona/Kumamoto/Germany diversification reduces single-region exposure. De-rating drivers: (1) Apple SF2 dual-source compresses HPC pricing power -> P/E re-rates toward 18-22x; (2) Intel 18A external traction breaks foundry monopoly assumption; (3) M6 Taiwan-strait fires and SOX-wide re-rate hits TSM hardest in the index (largest MSCI EM and MSCI Taiwan weight); (4) TSM ADR vs local Taiwan listing premium compression on foreign ownership flows. The valuation conclusion: TSM is paying for monopoly-AI-leverage at current price, which is rational IF both monopoly legs (I4 wafer + I6 packaging) stay intact, but offers limited margin of safety if either inflects.

27903398de6f482d94a6ee556331fd9f.title: TSMC - Capital return policy
27903398de6f482d94a6ee556331fd9f.body: TSMC capital return profile is structurally moderate for a monopoly: dividend yield ~1.5-2.0% (vs cycle-average 2.5-3%, compressed by P/E re-rating); historical payout ratio ~30-40% of consolidated earnings with steady quarterly dividend, no buyback program (Taiwan tax treatment historically disfavored buybacks vs dividends). FY26 capital priority is Arizona Fab 21 / 22 ramp (multi-year, doesn't contribute meaningfully to FCF before 2027-28), Kumamoto JV (operating but small), Germany Dresden JV (construction), and the AP6/AP7 Chiayi CoWoS expansion. Capex 2026 guide $42-44bn (~30-35% of revenue); FCF ~$25-35bn FY26 base case at $90-95bn revenue * 28-32% FCF margin. With no buyback, FCF flows to (1) dividend ~$15-18bn, (2) capex pre-funding (cash on balance sheet), (3) M&A optionality. Risk to capital return: (1) US-Taiwan tax treaty negotiations affecting cross-border dividend taxation; (2) Arizona facility cost overruns (Phase 1 already +50% vs original budget); (3) potential CFIUS/CHIPS Act conditions on capital deployment. The framework should treat TSM capital return as background-supportive (sustained dividend) but not a primary thesis driver - the thesis is the monopoly pricing power, not the cash flow distribution.

f28e25f018a141689f694730ad5f2cf1.title: SK Hynix (000660.KS) — anchor candidate
f28e25f018a141689f694730ad5f2cf1.body: SK Hynix (000660.KS) is the cleanest HBM pure-play in the universe: ~50-55% HBM3e bit-share at Nvidia for H200/B100/B200, 12-Hi shipping in volume, first to qualify HBM4 12-Hi (samples to Nvidia in 2025, qualification Q4 2025 / Q1 2026, volume target H1 2026). HBM is ~40-50% of DRAM revenue by 2026 - the highest HBM-leverage in memory and therefore the cleanest upside if I1's allocation phase persists AND the cleanest downside if Samsung HBM3e 12-Hi qualifies at Nvidia in scale. Non-HBM DRAM (~50%) is levered to I2 commodity DRAM cycle; NAND (Solidigm consolidated, ~15-20% of revenue) is levered to I3 with eSSD/QLC AI bonus. Won/USD: ~80% USD-denominated revenue, ~50% Won-denominated COGS - 1% Won weakness = ~0.3-0.5% positive to operating profit. Capex 2024-2026 is structurally HBM-tilted (M14 / M14W / M16 + Cheongju M15X); Yongin cluster is multi-year and won't contribute meaningfully before 2027-2028. SKH is the highest-beta, highest-conviction memory long IF the framework reads I1 as still allocation-driven; it is the worst memory short setup if framework reads I1 as turning. The composite scoring framework places SKH at the top of the 6-candidate ranking on cycle-leverage and AI-leverage, mid on geopol-discount (Wuxi China DRAM is licensed but renewable-risk), and mid on valuation (current ~1.8-2.0x P/B vs cycle mid 1.2-1.4x implies HBM premium is priced).

92b211ed10524d7ebece61d39aaa617b.title: Synthesis: SK Hynix captures the chain
92b211ed10524d7ebece61d39aaa617b.body: SK Hynix is the single asset that mechanically converts the I1 HBM allocation phase into reported earnings, with no business-mix dilution: ~50-55% Nvidia HBM3e share + first-to-HBM4 means M1 (AI accelerator unit demand growth >25% YoY) and M2 (HBM allocation persists) transmit into HBM revenue at $15-25/Gb vs commodity $3-4/Gb, which lands directly in DRAM operating profit (HBM gross margin 50%+ vs commodity 25-30%). The transmission is linear: every percentage point of incremental Nvidia GPU+ASIC ship growth multiplies through HBM-per-accelerator (150-200 GB blended, rising) into Hynix's allocated HBM3e/HBM4 bit-output, which clears at firm ASP because Samsung is still chasing 12-Hi qualification at Nvidia. The single-sentence chain: M1 AI demand -> HBM bit-demand >50% YoY vs SKH HBM supply ~35-40% YoY -> SKH HBM revenue >55% of DRAM at 50%+ HBM GM -> SKH DRAM operating profit +30%+ YoY FY26 -> SKH P/B holds 1.8-2.0x vs commodity-cycle 1.2-1.4x. The inversion chain (Samsung HBM3e 12-Hi at Nvidia in volume) breaks every link simultaneously, which is the structural reason SKH is binary on a single qualification event.

Consolidated FY26 revenue growth tracks ~25-30% YoY at base case. b80624c221d244e3be856383a3794e69.title: SK Hynix - Margin drivers
b80624c221d244e3be856383a3794e69.body: SKH FY26 operating margin bridge: HBM gross margin ~50%+ (vs commodity DRAM 25-30%, NAND 15-20%) is the engine. 5373229310e749f2838d1c30be140fe9.title: SK Hynix - Multiple / re-rating drivers
5373229310e749f2838d1c30be140fe9.body: SKH trades at ~1.8-2.0x trailing P/B vs cycle-mid 1.2-1.4x and cycle-trough ~0.8x - implying the market is paying ~40-60% premium to mid-cycle for the HBM-leverage. The P/B-vs-cycle frame matters more for SKH than P/E, because (a) EPS swings 5-10x peak-to-trough so P/E is structurally noisy, (b) P/B is a cleaner read on cycle position and structural ROE shift. Re-rating drivers: (1) HBM-leverage premium - if HBM stays >50% of DRAM revenue at 50%+ GM, SKH structural ROE re-rates from cycle-average 12-15% to 22-25%, justifying 1.8-2.0x P/B as fair-value; (2) HBM4 first-mover (volume 2H26) extends the HBM-leverage premium 12-18 months; (3) Korean discount compression as KOSPI memory cohort re-rates relative to S&P semis. De-rating drivers: (1) Samsung HBM3e 12-Hi at Nvidia in scale compresses HBM-leverage premium toward zero; (2) cycle-roll evidence (DRAM -3% MoM 3 consecutive months) pulls P/B back to cycle-mid 1.2-1.4x; (3) Wuxi China DRAM license non-renewal strips ~10-15% off NAV. The valuation-framework conclusion: SKH is paying for HBM-leverage at current price, which is rational IF I1 stays in allocation phase, but offers zero margin of safety if I1 inflects.

8ca615c2aad74a5b9e41ac833e22cc34.title: SK Hynix - Capital return policy
8ca615c2aad74a5b9e41ac833e22cc34.body: SKH capital return profile is structurally weaker than US peers because (a) Korean conglomerate capital allocation norms favor reinvestment over distribution, (b) HBM capex intensity (~30-35% of revenue at peak) absorbs FCF, (c) chaebol-related strategic considerations (SK Group) influence capital decisions. Dividend yield ~1-1.5% (vs MU ~0% and Samsung 005930 ~2-3%); historical buyback activity sporadic and small. The FY26 capital priority is Yongin cluster (multi-year, doesn't contribute before 2027-2028) + M14W and M15X expansion (HBM-tilted). Cash generation in cycle-peak FY26 (~KRW 30-40trn FCF base case at 32-36% OpM) opens optionality for incremental buyback or special dividend, but the framework should NOT base-case material capital return. Korean Value-Up program (announced 2024) provides some structural impulse but SKH has been slower than POSCO and Korean banks to commit. Comparison: MU runs CHIPS Act money through US-domestic capex with a clear path to FCF normalization and buybacks 2027+; SKH is structurally lower-yield.

c68b9f312c6d48c2aaf7adcd14fcfc61.title: Nvidia (NVDA) — anchor candidate
c68b9f312c6d48c2aaf7adcd14fcfc61.body: Nvidia is the framework's anchor merchant-silicon AI accelerator name and the single asset that mechanically captures M1 (AI accelerator unit demand) + M2 (HBM allocation phase) + I6 (advanced packaging bottleneck via 60-65% of CoWoS-L pool) + I7 (fabless merchant-silicon share). Product cycle Q4 FY26 base: Hopper (H100/H200) tail ~1.0M units FY26 (declining from ~1.5M FY25); Blackwell B200 SXM the volume SKU at ~1.3-1.6M FY26 units, B300 (Blackwell Ultra, 288GB HBM3e, 50% more HBM/unit than B200) ~600-900k FY26 units, GB200 NVL72 racks ~50-70k FY26, GB300 NVL72 ~30-50k racks FY26 (the flagship rack-scale platform); Rubin (R100, 384GB HBM4, 8x48GB stacks, ~1.5kW TDP) pre-orders FY26 H2 with HVM ramp FY27. Datacenter revenue $130-160bn FY26 base case (vs ~$95bn FY25), datacenter GM 74-78% (Priya base 76%; consensus midpoint), networking $ 13-16% of DC revenue (Spectrum-X + NVLink switches; rising as rack-scale GB300 NVL72 deploys at scale). Customer concentration: top-4 ~46% FY25 (MSFT + META + GOOG + AMZN cumulative), broadening with ORCL/Stargate/G42/Humain. Software/CUDA moat: ROCm parity gap closing slowly (AMD MI350+ROCm-7 is the canary - if hyperscalers report developer-time-to-port to ROCm <2x CUDA equivalent, moat compresses). Risks specific to NVDA: (1) Datacenter GM compression as AMD competes + custom silicon expands; (2) Customer-concentration shift to sovereign mega-deals (Stargate, Humain) which carry extension/cancellation risk; (3) Export control tightening (H20 effectively ended Apr-25, $5-6bn FY25 China revenue gone, ~$8bn FY26 H20+ banned trajectory); (4) Rubin yield / HBM4 ramp dependent on Hynix qualification; (5) CoWoS-L allocation politics (Nvidia 60-65% of pool, AMD pushing for higher share for MI350+). The composite scoring: NVDA clears top-1 ranking on AI-leverage + share-position + cycle, but offers thinnest margin of safety on valuation (~30-35x fwd P/E vs framework cohort average ~26x).

Blackwell/Rubin HBM intensity drives I1 allocation politics
TSMC N3/N2 leading-edge wafer pull is the upstream of NVDA chip supply
Export controls cap China-addressable NVDA revenue (H20 banned Apr-25)

146d6e8847124b7db87b414aa8497352.title: Synthesis: Nvidia captures the chain
146d6e8847124b7db87b414aa8497352.body: NVDA is the single asset that mechanically converts M1 (AI accelerator unit demand) + I7 (fabless merchant-silicon dominance) into reported earnings via the most direct demand-to-P&L chain in the framework. The transmission: M1 hyperscaler-5 capex $450-525bn FY26 with 55-65% AI-specific share -> $260-330bn accelerator $ TAM -> Nvidia ~65-75% share of merchant wallet (declining 4-6pts/yr to custom) -> $130-160bn DC revenue FY26 base -> DC GM 76% midpoint -> ~$100bn DC gross profit -> blended GM 73% -> OpM 60-62% -> FY26 EPS ~$5.50-6.20 (Priya base; consensus $5.80) -> P/E 30-35x defensible = $165-220 share price band. The single-sentence chain: hyperscaler capex >$420bn FY26 + custom-silicon share rising only 4-6pts -> NVDA DC rev $130-160bn at GM 74-78% -> EPS $5.50-6.20 -> P/E 30-35x defensible into cycle peak. The inversion chain (DC GM <72% OR AMD MI350 >700k OR custom share rises >10pts OR Rubin HBM4 delays) breaks both volume and margin legs simultaneously - which is why NVDA is more binary than its top-1-in-cohort ranking implies.

M1 macro AI accelerator demand is the top-down anchor

b991c569e4774fa6bc157bc74fd5ff26.title: Nvidia - Multiple / re-rating drivers
b991c569e4774fa6bc157bc74fd5ff26.body: NVDA trades at ~30-35x fwd NTM P/E (vs SOX cohort ~26x and 10Y NVDA mean ~28x; framework cohort average ~26x). Priya's read: market paying ~10-25% premium for AI-leverage + CUDA moat + Rubin product-cycle visibility. P/E frame for NVDA is cycle-aware but with growth-multiple anchoring (EPS cyclicality 3-4x peak-to-trough vs memory 5-10x). Re-rating drivers: (1) DC GM holding >76% structurally re-rates GP stream to higher steady-state multiple; (2) Rubin ramp delivers FY27 visibility; (3) Sovereign demand broadens customer base reducing concentration discount; (4) Custom-silicon share rises <5pts/yr removing bear narrative. De-rating drivers: (1) AMD MI350+ ramp >500k = competition repricing; (2) Custom share +10pts/yr = TAM compression; (3) Export controls tighten further on H20-successor SKUs; (4) Software-moat compression as ROCm-7 closes developer-time-to-port gap; (5) Top-4 customer concentration >55% = oligopsony risk premium. Valuation conclusion: NVDA pays for AI-monopoly at current price, rational IF DC GM 74-78% + custom share drift 4-6pts/yr hold; thinnest margin of safety in cohort but highest absolute earnings power. Base case PT $145 = $5.80 EPS * 25x fwd P/E (de-rate from cycle peak); bull $200 = $6.20 EPS * 32x; bear $95 = $4.80 EPS * 20x (binary fires).

34db6e865ce84e3f976dac3bd641b172.title: ASML (ASML.NA) — anchor candidate
34db6e865ce84e3f976dac3bd641b172.body: ASML is the framework's anchor equipment monopoly + the cleanest single-stock expression of the WFE cycle through the EUV intensity transmission channel: every leading-edge logic node bump (N3 -> N2 -> A16) requires 1.5-2x more EUV tools, every advanced DRAM node (1c/1d) adds incremental EUV layers, every High-NA-eligible critical layer at A16/A14 is a future EXE:5000 placement. 2026 base: revenue guided EUR30-35bn (midpoint EUR32.5bn vs EUR27.6bn 2024 / EUR28.4bn 2025), backlog end-Q1 2026 EUR40bn+, gross margin guided ~52-53% (compressing from 2023 peak as High-NA early shipments at lower mix-margin), operating margin ~33-34%. Revenue mix: EUV ~55%, DUV ~40%, metrology/applications ~5%. Tool ASP economics: NXE:3800E ~EUR220m (real customer throughput 180-200 wph vs 220 spec, 5-7 EUV layers per N3 wafer / 12-15 layers per N2), EXE:5000 ~EUR380m (5-7 systems shipping 2026, real throughput 100-130 wph vs 195 spec, ramp economics fragile and node-dependent). DUV (~40% of revenue): ~30% China-bound under grey-zone export controls, ASML China revenue normalized to ~28% in 2025 from 49% peak 2023 and finding a new floor. Quasi-monopoly position: no real competitor in EUV (SMEE in China is years behind on 0.33 NA, decades behind on 0.55 NA), 80%+ DUV market share, 80%+ scanner+coater pairing with TEL. Risks specific: (1) High-NA productivity stuck at 100-130 wph through 2027 cuts ASP uplift; (2) China DUV revenue re-tightens under new export controls; (3) WFE cycle decelerates below current backlog pace; (4) memory recovery slower than Park models. Composite scoring: ASML clears top-3 ranking on monopoly + AI-leverage + cycle + valuation, with the highest-quality monopoly story but the most consensus-loved position in the cohort.

d78c2bdb385148b2aa393efd5fcd59ad.title: Synthesis: ASML captures the chain
d78c2bdb385148b2aa393efd5fcd59ad.body: ASML is the single asset that mechanically converts M4 (bifurcated fab utilization, leading-edge tight) + AI-driven node-transition intensity into reported earnings via a 9-15 month book-to-revenue lag. The transmission: every TSMC/Samsung/Intel leading-edge wafer-start increment + every DRAM-maker EUV-layer increment + every High-NA-eligible critical layer adds tool orders that hit ASML bookings, settle into backlog, and convert to revenue 9-15 months later at GM 52-53%. The single-sentence chain: M1 AI accelerator demand -> hyperscaler-5 $420bn capex -> leading-edge wafer pull at TSMC N3/N2 and DRAM 1c/1d at Samsung/Hynix/MU -> EUV intensity rises (N3 uses 5-7 EUV layers, N2 uses 12-15, A16 adds High-NA layers) -> ASML EUV bookings >EUR3bn/Q -> FY27 ASML revenue EUR35bn+ at 53% GM -> ASML FY27 EPS +20% YoY -> P/E 32-35x defensible into cycle peak. The inversion chain (High-NA stuck at 100-130 wph through 2027 OR China DUV revenue compresses <20% OR cycle bookings roll <EUR4bn/Q) breaks every link via the cycle deceleration mechanism. The structural ASML advantage vs TSMC: ASML monopoly is not contingent on a single customer (TSMC's Apple risk), it is technology-monopoly with no second source in EUV; the risk is cycle timing + High-NA economics + China overhang, not competitive displacement.

M4 macro bifurcated utilization is the top-down anchor

Chain integrity decision propagates to ASML composite scoring

e233ce1c2ed94f0f9c452c483f00fa55.body: ASML FY26 revenue bridge EUR30-35bn (midpoint EUR32.5bn): EUV revenue ~55% (EUR17-18bn) split between NXE:3800E (~45-55 systems shipped at EUR220m ASP ~ EUR10-12bn) + EXE:5000 High-NA (~6 systems at EUR380m ASP ~ EUR2.3bn) + service/upgrades ~EUR4-5bn; DUV ~40% (EUR12-14bn) split between TWINSCAN immersion (~50% of DUV, ~EUR6-7bn including China grey-zone tools) and dry ArF / KrF / i-line (~50%, ~EUR6-7bn); metrology/applications ~5% (~EUR1.5-2bn). Growth drivers: (1) High-NA shipment ramp 2 systems 2024 -> 5-7 2026 -> 10-15 2027 adds EUR1-2bn/yr at ASP uplift; (2) memory EUV revenue rising from ~10% of EUV mix to 20-25% (DRAM 1c/1d adoption); (3) China DUV stabilizing at ~28% of revenue vs 49% peak (no further compression in base case). c730dc55639e4e088fc96d3946781219.title: ASML - Margin drivers
c730dc55639e4e088fc96d3946781219.body: ASML FY26 GM guided 52-53% (vs 51.3% FY24 / 51.8% FY25e), OpM ~33-34% on revenue EUR32.5bn midpoint = ~EUR11bn operating profit. The GM bridge: EUV tools 55-58% GM (NXE:3800E mature; EXE:5000 lower at first units 45-50% then ramping toward 55%); DUV 50-52% GM (mature); service/installed-base management 45-50% GM and growing as fleet expands. Mix-shift effects: (a) EUV % rising from 55% to 58% lifts blended GM ~50bps; (b) High-NA first units drag GM 100-150bps in FY26 (mix dilution) but should accrete from FY27 as throughput improves and ASP holds; (c) service revenue compounding ~20% YoY adds 100bps to GM trajectory through FY27. Cost levers: (1) Veldhoven manufacturing capacity expansion (EUR3bn investment 2022-26) leveraged through FY26; (2) Hermes Microvision (e-beam metrology) and Cymer (DUV sources) margin contribution; (3) FX (EUR/USD) - ASML reports in EUR with ~75% USD revenue, so EUR strength is a margin headwind. Risks: (1) High-NA mix drag persists (productivity stays low, ASP under pressure) = -100bps GM; (2) DUV mix shifts toward lower-margin China-tier tools = -50bps; (3) EUR/USD strengthens below 1.05 = -100bps GM.

d4a96742ffe447f7af269c03bc357ec9.title: ASML - Multiple / re-rating drivers
d4a96742ffe447f7af269c03bc357ec9.body: ASML trades at ~32-35x fwd P/E vs 10Y mean ~28x and cycle-trough ~18x - implying the market is paying ~15-25% premium to mean for the EUV monopoly + High-NA optionality + memory EUV broadening. The P/E-vs-cycle frame is appropriate (ASML EPS cyclicality ~3-4x peak-to-trough, similar to TSMC, lower than memory). Re-rating drivers: (1) High-NA productivity ramping toward 150+ wph by 2027 unlocks ASP-uplift narrative -> structural ROE step-up from 25% to 30% justifying 32-35x as fair-value; (2) memory EUV mix rising from 10% to 25%+ broadens revenue base and reduces logic-cycle dependence; (3) China DUV stabilizing (rather than re-compressing) removes the largest 2024-25 overhang. De-rating drivers: (1) High-NA productivity stuck at 100-130 wph -> ASP-uplift narrative dies -> P/E re-rates toward 25-28x; (2) China DUV re-tightens -10pp = -EUR3bn revenue = P/E compression toward 25x; (3) cycle bookings roll <EUR4bn/Q for 2Q = forward revenue cuts = P/E compression to 18-22x. The valuation conclusion: ASML is the highest-quality monopoly in equipment with the most consensus-loved positioning - which means the premium is being paid but the asymmetric risk is downside given crowded positioning.

44159ec123164752bdb40c31bb8cd036.title: ASML - Capital return policy
44159ec123164752bdb40c31bb8cd036.body: ASML capital return profile is structurally stronger than TSMC: dividend yield ~1.0-1.3% (modest by yield but with annual growth) PLUS a EUR12bn share buyback program announced Nov 2022 (~10% of market cap), active through 2025 and renewed through 2027. FY26 capital priorities: (1) capex ~EUR1.5-2bn (Veldhoven HQ + ramp investments, much lower than peers given fab-light model); (2) R&D ~EUR4-5bn (most expensive in WFE, justified by EUV + High-NA monopoly maintenance); (3) buyback ~EUR3-4bn/yr at current pace; (4) dividend ~EUR2.5-3bn/yr growing 5-10% YoY. FCF generation FY26 ~EUR8-10bn at EUR32.5bn revenue, leaving ~EUR3-4bn of optionality after dividend + buyback. The buyback is the differentiator: ASML actively reduces share count ~3-4% per year, compounding EPS growth above revenue growth. Risks: (1) EU-NL government 'national champion' status could constrain capital decisions (sovereign pressure on dividend/buyback in geopol scenario); (2) capex step-up for hypothetical 'High-NA-2' (next-gen 0.55+ NA) could absorb FCF; (3) US Trump-2.0 export control pressure on ASML capital deployment to China-tier service operations. The framework should treat ASML capital return as a primary thesis support (not background) given the buyback compounding effect on EPS through cycle peaks.

8505fb52eefc4e93a1bca7ea1512d925.title: Micron (MU) — anchor candidate
8505fb52eefc4e93a1bca7ea1512d925.body: Micron (MU) is the diversified memory pure-play with the cleanest US-political exposure: ~25% HBM mix targeted by FY26-FY27 (HBM3e 8-Hi shipped to Nvidia from early 2024, 12-Hi 2025, HBM4 sampling late 2025 / 2026), DRAM ~55% of revenue with 1-beta EUV node at Hiroshima, and NAND ~20% with stronger commodity-cycle leverage than SKH (no Solidigm aggregation). CHIPS Act money funds Boise (Idaho) R&D + pilot ramp, Hiroshima leading-node DRAM, and Clay (NY) future fab (2027+, multi-year build). The framework reads MU as the more diversified, less-binary memory long: lower HBM upside than SKH (~25% mix vs ~40-50%) but lower Samsung-qualification downside, plus structural US-political tailwind if US-China memory decoupling accelerates. Capacity at Taichung F16 (HBM3e) and Hiroshima provides flexibility; Manassas legacy DRAM is mature-node. Composite scoring frames MU as mid-pack on cycle-leverage (less concentrated than SKH), top-3 on AI-leverage (HBM exposure rising fast), top-2 on geopol-discount (US-domestic CHIPS beneficiary, not exposed to Korea-China-North Korea risk), and mid on valuation (P/E ~10-12x trailing on FY25 normalized vs SKH P/B premium framework). MU is the framework's choice for memory-cohort diversification vs SKH and Samsung Memory.

The framework reads MU as offering ~70-80% of the SKH upside with ~40-50% of the binary-downside, making it the right diversification choice for the memory book.

d7f5f0d4ecbf423e9ec9c1d88a677b9d.body: Broadcom is the framework's anchor custom-ASIC + networking-silicon name and the cleanest single-stock expression of the custom-silicon $-share-gain trajectory (I7 sub-track C). AI ASIC franchise wins: (1) Google TPU v5/v6/v7 - AVGO is co-designer for all three generations, manufactured on TSMC N3/N2; estimated $12-18bn FY26 AVGO TPU revenue; (2) Meta MTIA v2/v3 - AVGO partner on packaging + networking; $4-7bn FY26; (3) ByteDance ASIC via AVGO design services (subject to export-control complexity); $2-4bn FY26; (4) Apple AI server-class ASIC (emerging, FY27 production); (5) New customers - OpenAI custom silicon under exploration. Networking silicon: Tomahawk 5/6 (51.2T switching), Jericho 3-AI (deep buffer switching for AI clusters), AVGO PHY + optics; 65%+ market share in datacenter switching silicon. AI ASIC GM ~65% (vs merchant GPU 75%; ASIC margins lower because customer captures more value); networking GM ~70%. Composite scoring: AVGO clears top-3 ranking on AI-leverage + diversification + capital-return discipline (ex-VMware: high FCF conversion + dividend growth).

57ac62616009427f861f795dbb755abf.title: Synthesis: Broadcom captures the chain
57ac62616009427f861f795dbb755abf.body: AVGO is the single asset that mechanically converts M1 (AI accelerator demand) + I7 custom-silicon sub-track C into reported earnings via the custom-ASIC value-share channel. The transmission: M1 hyperscaler-5 capex $450-525bn FY26 -> $260-330bn accelerator $ TAM -> custom-silicon $ share rising 4-6pts/yr (base 32-37% FY26) -> $80-120bn custom-silicon $ available -> AVGO ~25-35% share of custom (TPU + MTIA + ByteDance ASIC) = $20-40bn AI ASIC revenue -> AI ASIC GM 63-67% -> AI gross profit ~$13-26bn -> blended consolidated GM 63-65% (including software at GM ~85%) -> OpM 45-48% -> FY26 EPS ~$8-10 (Priya base; consensus $8.50-9.00) -> P/E 24-28x defensible = $200-280 share price band. The single-sentence chain: hyperscaler capex >$420bn + custom-silicon share rising 4-6pts/yr -> AVGO AI ASIC rev $20-30bn FY26 at GM 65% -> EPS $8-10 -> P/E 24-28x. The inversion chain (TPU v7 slip OR Google concentration spike OR networking share loss OR Apple captive transition) breaks the AI franchise leg - but unlike NVDA, AVGO retains networking + VMware + legacy semi as defensive ballast, so AVGO is less binary than NVDA on a single metric.

3786904719c941f7835f602f530d41f5.title: Broadcom - Revenue drivers
3786904719c941f7835f602f530d41f5.body: AVGO FY26 revenue bridge: AI ASIC + networking ($32-38bn, ~54% of consolidated) +45-60% YoY driven by (1) GOOG TPU v7 (Ironwood) ramp from late FY26, partial revenue $5-8bn; (2) TPU v6 (Trillium) volume year, ~$8-10bn; (3) META MTIA v2 scaling + v3 launch FY26 H2, $4-7bn; (4) ByteDance ASIC + emerging customers $2-4bn; (5) Networking silicon (Tomahawk 6, Jericho 3-AI, optics) +30% YoY at $10-12bn. Legacy semi ($22-28bn, ~36% of consolidated) 0-5% YoY: broadband (modem + WiFi 7) flat, server storage +5%, industrial flat-to-down. Software ($20-22bn, ~33% of total revenue but here treated under semi-pure-play consolidation): VMware integration year - cost restructure delivering, license migration to subscription model, $10-12bn FY26 OP contribution. Consolidated FY26 revenue ~$80bn (semi ~$60bn + software ~$22bn vs FY25 ~$70bn). Single largest swing variable is TPU v7 ramp - $3-8bn band; second is networking silicon share - 60-70% band drives $2-3bn revenue delta. Risks: (1) Google concentration risk - any TPU strategy shift; (2) Custom-ASIC competition from MRVL (AWS) and Alchip (other hyperscalers); (3) FX - USD strength.

4b7f63e2a50f41289d1c07895da9d3a6.body: AVGO FY26 OpM bridge: Semi blended GM 63-65% with AI ASIC GM ~65% + networking GM ~70% + legacy semi GM ~60%; software (VMware) GM ~85% lifting consolidated blended GM to 75-77%. Margin levers: (1) AI ASIC mix-shift from 30% to 50% of semi grows GM 100-150bps; (2) VMware integration cost-restructure ($10bn+ run-rate savings target) delivering FY26 = ~300bps consolidated OpM accretion; (3) Networking high-incremental-GM (Tomahawk 6/J3) scaling; (4) Subscription-mix-shift on VMware enables price uplift + margin defense. Risks: (1) AI ASIC GM pressure as competition emerges (MRVL Trainium share-gain pressuring AVGO); (2) TSMC N3/N2 ASP pass-through to customers - if AVGO can't pass cost to GOOG/META, 200bps GM compression; (3) VMware customer churn from license-to-subscription migration; (4) Legacy semi destock - if industrial worsens, -50bps GM. 966aaee641874b32843618f2debf1ffa.title: Broadcom - Multiple / re-rating drivers
966aaee641874b32843618f2debf1ffa.body: AVGO trades at ~24-28x fwd NTM P/E (vs SOX cohort ~26x and 10Y AVGO mean ~18x; pre-VMware mean ~20x). Priya's read: market paying premium for AI ASIC custom-silicon share-gain + VMware synergy capture + diversification. P/E frame is cycle-aware but with growth-multiple anchoring; AVGO EPS cyclicality lower than NVDA because legacy semi + software ballast (peak-to-trough 2-3x vs NVDA 3-4x). Re-rating drivers: (1) AI ASIC share rising +6pts/yr structurally re-rates to higher steady-state multiple; (2) VMware synergy capture on plan delivers FY26-27 EPS visibility; (3) Hock Tan capital allocation track record (consistent buyback + dividend growth); (4) Networking franchise resilience. De-rating drivers: (1) Google concentration risk (>40% of AI ASIC); (2) Apple captive transition; (3) TPU v7 ramp slip; (4) MRVL share-gain on AWS Trainium displaces AVGO addressable market. Valuation conclusion: AVGO offers better risk-adjusted return than NVDA (lower binary risk, dividend yield 1.5-2%, diversification ballast) but lower upside (single-customer concentration cap). Base case PT $260 = $9 EPS * 28x; bull $310 = $10 EPS * 31x; bear $180 = $7 EPS * 25x.

e1e7a3a956a243b49b43af2b7a19be4b.body: AVGO capital return profile is the strongest in the framework cohort: dividend yield ~1.5-2.0% with 10%+ YoY dividend growth historically (FY15-FY24 dividend CAGR ~37% pre-VMware), $30bn buyback authorization (refreshed post-VMware), payout ratio ~30-40% of FCF. Capital priority: (1) Dividend growth ~10% YoY (Hock Tan track record); (2) VMware integration debt paydown ($30bn+ consolidated debt, target investment-grade-strong rating, paydown $8-10bn/yr); (3) Buyback $5-10bn FY26; (4) Strategic M&A optionality (next platform deal in 3-5 years). FCF margin structurally supports dividend growth + buyback + debt paydown simultaneously. Risks: (1) VMware integration cost overruns; (2) AI ASIC capex requirements (substrate deposits, mask set investments) pressuring FCF; (3) Acquisition risk (Hock Tan track record of transformative deals - could be value-accretive or value-destructive depending on target). The framework treats AVGO capital return as PRIMARY thesis driver (unlike NVDA where it's background-supportive) because dividend + buyback compounding contributes 4-5%/yr to total return.

032a543f1b104b198da271544e6df4e2.title: Hedge: SOX index sector-beta neutralizer
032a543f1b104b198da271544e6df4e2.body: SOX sector-beta hedge: short the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) or buy a 3M 95/85 put-spread on SOXX (iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF) to neutralize beta on the single-name long book during BIS publication windows and Q-earnings clusters where idiosyncratic alpha is structurally suppressed by sector tape. Construction: when book gross-long exposure is 18-22% NAV across TSMC/ASML/NVDA/AVGO/Hynix/MU, sell 30-50% beta-equivalent SOXX (SOXX 30D realized beta to SOX is ~0.99; book composite beta to SOX is ~1.2-1.4 with NVDA/AVGO weight). Carry cost: SOXX has zero borrow on most prime broker books; 3M 95% put-spread costs ~1.5-2.5% of notional (skew elevated at SOX +30% YTD); preferred structure is SOXQ 3M 95/85 put-spread for +200-300bp NAV protection at -8 to -12% SOX moves with capped downside. Active when: (a) Sarah's geopol calendar shows BIS rule window <30 days; (b) Pillar-4 lead signals show 2+ tripwires elevated; (c) book gross exceeds 22% NAV. Reserve when: (a) base case tracking 3+/5 confirmed signals; (b) SOX implied vol <22%; (c) earnings clusters >2 weeks out. Sizing: 50-100bp NAV premium budget per quarter.

6ce8746838b14440a21ae6314f466830.body: Taiwan-Strait risk premium overlay: long Taiwan sovereign 5Y CDS (currently 28-42bp spread, moves to 80-150bp on coercion scenarios per RAND/CSIS playbooks) and/or TAIEX OTM put spreads (3M, 10-15% OTM). The CDS leg carries flat (premium = annual running spread = 28-42bp on $20M = $56-84k/yr) and is the cleanest sovereign-risk instrument; the TAIEX put leg captures the equity dislocation (TAIEX -25 to -40% on full blockade per CSIS 'First Battle' wargame, Bloomberg Economics Jan 2024 model -10% global GDP scenario). Marine cargo insurance premium tracker (Lloyd's published, baseline ~$2.5/$1000 cargo value) is the highest-cadence leading signal - >2x baseline = first warning, >5x = scenario_stress firing. Active when: PLA exercise tempo elevated (Joint Sword 2024A/B precedent) OR Taiwan election cycle <90 days OR US-Taiwan defense announcement window. Reserve when: ADIZ incursion count <baseline AND no Strait political flashpoint <60 days.

55a53cb15a954c29a5b51ff82931774d.title: Hedge: aggregate hedge-book stop-loss (-3% NAV/quarter)
55a53cb15a954c29a5b51ff82931774d.body: Aggregate hedge-book stop-loss: -3% NAV/quarter composite drawdown on the hedge stack itself triggers stack re-architecture. Rationale: hedges are insurance with running cost; if they bleed >3% NAV in a single quarter, either (a) the underlying risk being hedged never materialized (consistent over-hedging - book is paying for protection it does not need), or (b) the hedge structure is wrong for the actual risk regime (e.g., put-spreads vs outright shorts, calls vs forwards). Both cases require structural review, not just sizing adjustment. Composite tracking: weekly P&L attribution per hedge leg (SOX put-spread / Taiwan CDS / SMIC pair / KRW NDF / TWD call-spread), with quarterly aggregate vs prior 3Q average. If trailing-quarter hedge stack P&L < -3% NAV, all 4 active legs reviewed for (i) instrument substitution (e.g., NDF instead of options), (ii) sizing recalibration (reduce 30-50% notional), or (iii) leg unwind. The stop also enforces discipline against letting hedge legs become 'permanent expenses' - a known anti-pattern in long-only portfolios where hedge premium runs without revisiting the underlying hedging case.

Stage 4 (resolution): blockade lifts; TSMC restart from wafer-in-process buffer ~2 weeks; customer scheduling chaos persists 2-3 quarters; CapEx pull-forward to AZ/JASM accelerates. The mechanism breaks I4 (logic monopoly), I6 (CoWoS), M5 (CoWoS expansion) for the duration; M1 (AI demand) survives if duration <4 weeks - hyperscaler training schedules slip but do not cancel.

M1 (AI accelerator demand): -10 to -15% FY26 shipment quantity (supply-broken, not demand-broken; recovers 1-2 quarters post-resolution); M5 (CoWoS expansion): breaks for duration (2-4 weeks) + 2-3Q customer-scheduling chaos; I4 (leading-edge logic): TSMC monthly revenue -15 to -25% for 1-2 months; I6 (advanced packaging): full breakage of CoWoS supply for duration. Candidate-level impact: TSMC -25 to -40% (revenue + multiple compression); Nvidia -15 to -25% (CoWoS-dependent shipment break); AVGO -15 to -22% (networking + AI ASIC); ASML -12 to -18% (Taiwan service revenue exposure); SK Hynix -8 to -15% (less Taiwan-dependent but HBM-into-Nvidia indirect); Samsung -5 to -10%; Micron -3 to -8% (US-fab dominant). Cohort aggregate -15 to -25% first week then partial recovery. Recovery timeline: 2-3 quarters of customer-scheduling chaos post-resolution; CoWoS throughput catches up 3-4 quarters; long-term effect is acceleration of AZ Fab 21 Phase 2 + Phase 3 + Kumamoto Phase 2 + Dresden CapEx pull-forward.

Signal hierarchy: marine insurance + PLA tempo are the fastest leading indicators (days); TSMC monthly is the highest-conviction confirming (lagging by 30-40 days).

181305df09f24042b91739dfe6c70353.title: Mechanism: how it propagates
181305df09f24042b91739dfe6c70353.body: TAIL mechanism: causal propagation. Branch A (kinetic) - Stage 1 (Hours 0-48): Strait naval/air engagement OR missile strike on Taiwan infrastructure; Taiwan power grid stress; TSMC fab operations at risk regardless of fab being targeted (power infrastructure attacks trip Hsinchu/Tainan/Kaohsiung fab operations - wafer-in-process loss ~$20-50bn at any moment given TSMC monthly revenue $7-8bn at advanced-node mix). Stage 2 (Days 2-14): TSMC stated 'fab inoperability' / self-destruct protocols engage (veracity disputed - per Sarah Phase 1 open question 4); if protocols engage, fab restart timeline measured in years (rebuild + tool re-qualification + yield recovery). Stage 3 (Days 14+): global semis equities -40-60% drawdown; AI training programs halt for non-AZ-fabricated capacity; Nvidia/AMD/AVGO shipment chains broken indefinitely; restart pulls forward AZ Phase 2/3 + JASM Phase 2 + Dresden + Korean memory CapEx by 2-3 years. Branch B (maximalist BIS) - Stage 1 (Day 0): Rule publishes; H20 ($10-15bn Nvidia annualized) instant write-off; Korean memory Wuxi/Xi'an exposure repricing within hours. Stage 2 (Weeks 1-6): CXMT/YMTC commodity DRAM/NAND ramp accelerates (indigenous substitution); Korean memory makers (SKH, Samsung) re-evaluate Chinese operations (freeze, divest, or write-down); Nvidia data-center FY27 estimates cut $8-15bn. Stage 3 (Quarters 1-4): global memory ASP regime shifts as Chinese supply ramps; rare-earth + gallium retaliation follow-on cycle activates (Sarah Scenario F).

d2c705404a5a4392a9f759dddd552e00.title: Gap — where framework reading disagrees with consensus
d2c705404a5a4392a9f759dddd552e00.body: Where the framework reads disagree with consensus: (1) The 'AI is secular' narrative — framework regresses NVDA DC revenue growth on hyperscaler-5 capex YoY over trailing 8 quarters; the R² is materially above 0.6 with 1-2 quarter lag (sell-side will not run this comparison). NVDA is a high-beta capex-cycle stock, not a secular compounder — the 2000-02 CSCO/SUNW analog matters more than consensus admits. (2) 'HBM tightness lasts through 2027' — framework's bottoms-up HBM bit-supply model (Hynix + Samsung + MU stated capex + announced TSV adds + Park's yield curve work) suggests supply catches demand in 2H 2026, not 2027. The premium peaks in mid-2026 and starts compressing as Samsung qualification scales. (3) 'TSMC has monopoly pricing power at N2' — framework models N2 ASP $22k base / $25k bull / $19k bear vs consensus $25-28k. The right Q is whether Apple / NVDA dual-sources at all. (4) 'Equipment is a 2027 story' — ASML book-to-revenue lag is 9-15 months; 2025-26 bookings ARE 2026-27 revenue; equipment is already priced for the next cycle. The gap framework offers: explicit name-by-name sensitivities on each of these four divergences.

27b47b6ac09843f4b2f480c84d170ce1.body: Two competing narratives drive the 2026 tape: (1) the dominant Street narrative — 'AI is secular, decoupled from the semi cycle; NVDA / TSMC / Hynix / ASML are compounders, not cyclicals; the 2024-25 inventory recession is over and AI takes the relay'; (2) the framework's counter-narrative — 'Semis remain a 3-5 year capex-driven inventory cycle with an AI-accelerator overlay; the two cycles are now 9-12 months out of phase (AI pulled forward, commodity logic + analog still digesting); when they re-converge in 1H-2H 2026, the entire AI-as-secular framing breaks and the cohort de-rates'. The third narrative — 'sovereign AI is the new demand layer that decouples from hyperscaler capex' — is gaining sell-side currency but is unaudited; framework's task is to instrument sovereign demand (UAE G42, Saudi PIF, India, EU AI Factories) as a fragile incremental rather than a structural base. The narrative gap between framework and Street is binary on the cycle-vs-secular question — both frames cannot be right; resolution by Q4 2026 at latest.

Together these signal where the cycle is going before TSMC monthly revenue or fabless inventory prints confirm. Sell-side cadence: weekly review of (a)+(d)+(e), monthly review of (b), quarterly deep-dive on (c).

c293d98f953c460e83d15f8e9ae64898.title: Lag indicators (analog WoI, distributor channel, fabless inventory)
c293d98f953c460e83d15f8e9ae64898.body: Lag indicators are the diagnostic on inventory absorption — the cleanest read on whether the cycle exit is real or premature. The analog cohort destock has lasted longer than any cycle in 20 years; the framework holds that the lag prints are the high-conviction confirm. Cluster: (a) Top-50 semi WoI (mkt-cap weighted, FactSet/Compustat quarterly; >14wks glut, <8wks tight); (b) Analog cohort WoI — TXN, ADI, NXP, Infineon, STM, Microchip (10-Q quarterly; >18wks continued destocking); (c) Distributor B:B (Arrow, Avnet, WPG; leads producer B:B by ~1 quarter); (d) Fabless sell-in vs sell-through gap (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, QCOM, MRVL; >2 quarters of sell-in > sell-through = channel stuffing risk); (e) NVDA inventory + purchase commitments (purchase commitments / fwd revenue ratio = supply confidence proxy). These resolve slowest but with highest signal-to-noise; trust them more than the lead/coincident reads when the cycle is at an inflection.

3b900fdc6a1c43f8a07eeaf4a17495a3.title: Scheduled catalysts (BIS rule cadence, TSMC monthly, quarterly earnings)
3b900fdc6a1c43f8a07eeaf4a17495a3.body: Scheduled events drive the framework's calendar: every TSMC monthly revenue release (day 10 of each month), every BIS rule expected window (per Sarah's primary cadence), every quarterly earnings cycle (NVDA / TSMC / ASML / Hynix / MU / AVGO / AMD), every SEMI Billings Report (~3rd week lag of month-end), every SEMI World Fab Forecast quarterly update, every WSTS monthly print (~6wk lag), every TrendForce contract DRAM round (semi-annual). Add to that: Section 232 final rule expected mid-2026, Taiwan 2028 presidential election cycle starting to price 6-9M ahead (Sarah). The framework's edge is sequencing these — knowing which scheduled prints fire before which others lets us front-run the consensus reaction. Sell-side cadence: weekly review of upcoming month's scheduled calendar; pre-positioning before TSMC monthly + quarterly earnings (NVDA specifically, which moves the entire AI-fabless cohort by 5-10% on prints).

a3fcfb0f2bfd4bf0ab521d8605818832.body: Unscheduled events are the framework's tripwires for tail outcomes: (a) export-control surprise — BIS adds HBM-to-China rule outside the expected window, or new entity-list additions affecting Hynix/MU/TSMC China revenue; (b) Taiwan Strait incident — PLA exercise tempo escalation, US naval transit confrontation, marine cargo insurance premium spike >2x baseline; (c) NVDA or TSMC pre-announcement / mid-quarter guide cut (both have done this in prior cycles when channel deterioration outpaces calendar); (d) Korean / Taiwan currency shock — KRW or TWD vs USD swing >5% in a single week, moving Hynix/TSMC reported earnings 5-10%; (e) Sovereign AI cancellation — UAE/Saudi/India/EU sovereign program scaled back or cancelled, revealing speculative procurement; (f) Major hyperscaler capex revision mid-year (outside the scheduled earnings cycle). These are the events the framework can't time but must price via hedge architecture. Cadence: daily news scan + Sarah's escalation triggers + Korean/Taiwan financial press.

7c6b6012e60349d58515619d4e1daf67.body: Tripwires are the framework's pre-committed kill conditions — each is calibrated to a specific severity and a specific position-sizing response. Twelve listed in David's Phase-1 brief, ordered by frequency-of-firing and decision-impact: (1) TSMC monthly YoY <15% sustained 2M non-seasonal — WARNING; (2) Hyperscaler-5 aggregate capex revision <-5% in a season — KILL AI sub-thesis; (3) HBM ASP premium <3x DDR5 for 2Q — KILL HBM tightness; (4) DRAM spot DDR5 -3% MoM x3 — WARNING-to-KILL; (5) ASML EUV bookings <€2bn for 2Q — KILL equipment; (6) NA Equipment B:B <0.95 x3M — WARNING; (7) Analog cohort WoI >20 weeks — INFO/WARNING; (8) BIS HBM-to-China rule — KILL clean memory; (9) Section 232 tariff >15% — WARNING; (10) TSMC CoWoS capacity delay >1Q — INFO (net-neutral, repositions); (11) NVDA DC GM <70% — WARNING; (12) SOX fwd P/E >+2σ with EPS rev breadth <50% — WARNING. Each tripwire has a pre-committed action — the framework's discipline is to execute mechanically when the condition fires, before the cohort de-rates further.

fb8bb126af5b4aa1b0d0fec4707c4cfc.title: Cross-asset confirmers (KRW/TWD, US bond yields, copper, gold)
fb8bb126af5b4aa1b0d0fec4707c4cfc.body:
Cross-asset confirmers tell the framework whether the semi cycle's signals are unique or part of a broader risk-on/risk-off rotation. Critical pairs: (a) KRW/USD — Korean won is the cleanest single proxy for foreign-investor confidence in Hynix; >5% week swing moves reported earnings 5-10%; (b) TWD/USD — analogous for TSMC; Taiwan equity flows follow currency at <3% week threshold; (c) US 10Y bond yield + 2s10s — rising yields compress growth-stock multiples; SOX has -0.6 correlation to 10Y yields in trailing 3Y data; (d) Copper / industrial metals — leading indicator for industrial / auto end-demand recovery (analog cohort echo); (e) Gold + DXY — risk-off proxies; rising gold + rising DXY = flight-to-safety, semi cohort underperforms 5-10%; (f) Taiwan TAIEX semi sub-index NTD/USD-hedged return — when this underperforms SOX in USD terms despite earnings, Taiwan-specific risk premium is rising. Cadence: daily review of (a)-(c); weekly review of (d)-(f). Framework's use: if 3+ cross-asset confirmers flip risk-off in same week, downgrade conviction by one level even if semi-specific reads still positive.

Phase-5 additions (Priya + David Phase-4 critic reconciliation): three new observables added as primary children of this cross-asset node: (1) SOX P/B-vs-RoE z-score (monthly FactSet) - David Phase-1 instrument #3 - distinguishes multiple-driven vs EPS-driven rallies; (2) ORCL RPO QoQ growth (quarterly) - Priya recommendation - cleanest sovereign + Stargate flow-through demand signal; (3) Lloyd's Taiwan-Strait marine cargo + war-risk premium (weekly) - Priya + Sarah recommendation - cleanest grey-zone Taiwan disruption signal. The original 'gold' line item in the body is downweighted as macro noise for this thesis.

c478de8b64f6f867ef85579bc385d8db.title: Cycle-leverage attribute (mid- vs late-cycle exposure)
c478de8b64f6f867ef85579bc385d8db.body: Cycle-leverage attribute: each candidate must score on a 1-5 scale for where in the SOX cycle its underlying P&L sensitivity sits. (1 = late-cycle, full earnings-cliff exposure - e.g., commodity DRAM merchant on incremental supply; 5 = early/mid-cycle, multi-quarter earnings tailwind with secular over-write - e.g., HBM4 ramp into Rubin demand). The screen rewards 3-5 (mid+) and penalizes 1-2 (late). Operationalize via: book-to-bill 3M MA, inventory weeks-on-hand, capex/revenue ratio vs 3-year trailing average, ASP momentum 3M MA. David sell-side composite + Park memory mechanic deliver the inputs. The framework requires this attribute to be non-generic (reject 'low P/E' as cycle proxy - book-to-bill is more proximate).

f3d4c3750693afcad6fce2bb14e17532.title: Geopol-discount attribute (Taiwan + China exposure pricing)
f3d4c3750693afcad6fce2bb14e17532.body: Geopol-discount attribute: each candidate must score on a 1-5 scale for (a) Taiwan-Strait exposure (TSMC fab dependency, Taiwan revenue mix), (b) China revenue exposure (BIS rule sensitivity, FDPR risk, VEU status if applicable), and (c) consensus pricing of that exposure vs framework view. (1 = high Taiwan + high China + under-discounted in consensus - e.g., a name with 80% Taiwan-fab dependency trading at full-multiple parity with US-fab peer; 5 = low Taiwan + low China OR adequately discounted exposure - e.g., MU which is US-fab dominant, or TSMC where the 1-3x EV/EBITDA gap below US peers IS the discount). The screen rewards 3-5 (under-discounted exposure OR adequately priced) and penalizes 1-2 (mis-priced exposure). Operationalize via: % revenue Taiwan-fabbed (TSMC dependency), % revenue China end-use (BIS scope), peer-relative EV/EBITDA discount, and Sarah's scenario-stress P&L attribution per name.
